title: Match structure — best-of-3 + match-resolve banner + tally reset
notes: GDP-2026-05-22-014. Adds session shape to Kaboom Crew: 'match' = best-of-3 decisive rounds.
Other queued GDPs deferred: GDP-011 (MUST, server-authoritative gameplay) is multi-sprint; GDP-012 + GDP-013 are smaller follow-ups that fit after 011.

stories.title: Multiplayer Sprint B — server-authoritative bomb/blast/pickup/round-resolve (the headline cross-tab gameplay sync)
stories.summary:
S109 shipped Sprint A of GDP-2026-05-22-009 (connect-and-spectate): two tabs can connect, each sees the OTHER tab's bomber as a remote Presence entity with synced position + recipe. But each tab still runs its OWN bomb-fuse + blast-propagation + pickup + round-resolve locally — Tab A's bomb doesn't appear in Tab B's arena. The headline acceptance of GDP-2026-05-22-009 — 'Tab A places a bomb → Tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms; Tab A's bomb kills tab B's bomber; both tabs see the round resolve' — STILL pending. This is Sprint B: move bomb-fuse, blast-propagation, block-destruction, pickup-collect, pickup-spawn, round-resolve, bot-AI to the SERVER. Clients receive these as snapshot deltas + transient events. Local client systems for these become render/audio decorators that fire VFX/audio from the snapshot. The 'modern network game' from the user's 2026-05-20 ask FINALLY arrives.

Rationale:
GDP-2026-05-22-009 acceptance hints split this into Sprint A → D. Sprint A shipped (connect-and-spectate, recipe sync via Option B in S112). Sprint B is the user-visible payoff — without it, multiplayer is just a chatroom with avatars walking around, not a shared game. Sized as MUST because the rest of the multiplayer story (drop-in/out polish, snapshot relevance) is meaningless without cross-tab gameplay sync first. The architectural pieces are all in place: gameplay is grid-authoritative + deterministic + no Math.random/no wall-clock, exactly what the protocol contract expects. Sprint B is the integration sprint, not new design.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Builds on S109 connect-and-spectate (FEAT-MULTIPLAYER-FOUNDATION-T-001) + S112 recipe sync (FEAT-MP-RECIPE-SYNC-001).
  - Reference: existing docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md — extend with a Sprint B section before implementation. Spike sub-story may precede this if dev wants to derisk the server-side ECS port.
  - SERVER-SIDE (examples/backends/node-world-server, new kaboom-crew module):
  -   Kaboom Crew rules ship as a server-side module. Port these CLIENT systems to server-side equivalents that act on the authoritative ECS world:
  -     bomb-placement-system → validates PlaceBombRequest from client; spawns Bomb entity on server world
  -     bomb-fuse-system → ticks fuseRemaining on every server tick; emits BlastEvent at zero
  -     blast-propagation-system → walks the blast on the server; spawns BlastTile entities; flips alive=false on hit bombers (after Shield check); destroys soft blocks
  -     pickup-spawn-system → server-side RNG (seeded by world seed + cell) decides pickup drops
  -     pickup-collect-system → server detects bomber-cell-overlap; applies BomberStats updates
  -     round-resolve-system → server detects ≤1 bomber alive; flips RoundState.phase; bumps tally; auto-restart after 3s
  -     bot-AI-system → server owns bot decisions; empty player slots filled by bots
  -   Server runs at fixed tick rate (e.g. 30 Hz). Snapshots emit at ~10 Hz (configurable).
  -   Server seeds the arena from a per-world seed; pickup drops + bot decisions all use seeded RNGs — same world seed → same outcomes every time.
  - CLIENT-SIDE (examples/kaboom-crew):
  -   In 'connected' profile, DISABLE the local bomb-fuse / blast-propagation / pickup / round-resolve / bot-AI systems. They become server-only.
  -   Local systems that REMAIN client-side:
  -     player-input-system → reads keyboard, sends inputIntent to server
  -     grid-movement-system → client-prediction for LOCAL player only (remote players use interpolator)
  -     death-animation-system → reads alive-flip from snapshot, fires ragdoll locally with blast direction from snapshot's BomberDied event
  -     hit-recoil-system → reads shield-pop event from snapshot
  -     voice-synth + audio-fx → fire from server-event deltas
  -     HUD / minimap → reads from snapshot
  - PROTOCOL EXTENSIONS (schemas/protocol.schema.json):
  -   placeBombRequest { entityId, gx, gz }: client → server
  -   detonateRemoteRequest { entityId }: client → server (for Remote power-up)
  -   inputIntent { entityId, dx, dz, tick }: client → server (movement input)
  -   blastEvent { originGx, originGz, range, ownerId, cells: [{gx,gz}] }: server → client
  -   pickupCollected { entityId, kind, gx, gz }: server → client
  -   bomberDied { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz, killerId }: server → client
  -   shieldConsumed { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz }: server → client
  -   roundResolved { phase, winnerId?, tally, nextRoundAt }: server → client
  -   blockDestroyed { gx, gz, droppedPickupKind?: string }: server → client
  -   Each event opaque JSON; client decoder routes to local systems for VFX + audio.
  - CLIENT PREDICTION (movement only):
  -   Local player's GridMover updates apply immediately on input (predict).
  -   Server snapshot reconciles: if local grid position differs by ≤ 1 cell, smooth interp toward server value over 200 ms. If > 1 cell, snap. Remote players: interpolate via existing remote-bomber-interpolator-system.
  -   No prediction on bomb placement — client sends placeBombRequest, waits for server's spawnBomb in snapshot. ~100-200 ms perceived latency on placement is acceptable for arcade pace.
  - DETERMINISM:
  -   Server's RNG is the authority; clients trust snapshots. The existing bot-vs-bot regression test runs SERVER-SIDE and must continue to resolve within budget with bit-identical outcomes given the same world seed.
  -   Client-side visual interpolation may differ tab-to-tab — acceptable per gameplay-systems.md §12.1 (visual determinism not binding).
  - PROFILE WIRING:
  -   ?profile=connected → networked path (default for two-tab playtest)
  -   ?profile=static → local single-player offline (unchanged from today)
  -   ?world=<id> → which server world to join (default 'test')
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST (the headline that's been pending since 2026-05-20):
  -   Two Playwright tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected.
  -   Tab A controls player.1 (or auto-assigned), Tab B controls a second bomber.
  -   Tab A places a bomb → tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms.
  -   Tab A's bomb chains into Tab B's cell → tab B's bomber gets the ragdoll launch + the killer's recipe seed propagates correctly.
  -   Both tabs see the same RoundState (phase + tally + nextRoundAt).
  -   Auto-restart fires identically on both tabs (within snapshot jitter).
  - BOTS IN MULTIPLAYER:
  -   Server fills empty bomber slots with server-side bots. Each connected player gets a bomber, plus enough server-bots to fill to 4 total (configurable per world).
  -   Bot personality / difficulty per world config (server-side, NOT per-client).
  - DIAGNOSTICS:
  -   /__agf/network probe extends — peer count, last-snapshot bytes + latency, reconciliation jump count (already proposed in GDP-009).
  -   Doctor section: 'Connected profile: server reachable, snapshot rate, reconciliation events last 30s'.
  - ROLLBACK PLAN:
  -   If Sprint B reveals a perf or correctness issue blocking ship, the client retains the static profile path and the server skeleton stays available behind a feature flag. Connect-and-spectate (S109) keeps working as the multiplayer floor.
  - OUT OF SCOPE (Sprint C/D separately):
  -   Drop-in/out behaviour for joins-at-mid-round (spectate-until-next-round) — Sprint C in GDP-2026-05-22-012.
  -   5s reconnect grace on disconnect — Sprint C.
  -   Snapshot relevance filter — Sprint D (deferrable; current 15×11 arena fits whole snapshot).
  -   Lag compensation / hitscan rewind — no hitscan in this game.
  -   Server reconnect-resume after server restart.
  -   Custom rooms / lobbies / matchmaking.
  -   Authentication / anti-cheat.

Source proposal: GDP-2026-05-22-011 (kind=feature, priority=must)
stories.deferredReason: Multi-sprint scope (67 acceptance hints, 7 systems to move server-side). Needs its own dedicated sprint cycle. Re-promote when S115+ ships and the kaboom-crew arena is stable on the client.

stories.title: Multiplayer Sprint C — drop-in/out behaviour, 5s reconnect grace, spectate-until-next-round for mid-round joiners
stories.summary:
After Sprint B (GDP-2026-05-22-011) lands, the gameplay is shared between tabs but the JOIN / LEAVE behaviour is still abrupt: connecting mid-round drops the new player straight into the arena (where they're likely insta-killed by an in-flight blast), and disconnecting kills the bomber immediately even on a momentary network blip. Sprint C polishes the world-lifecycle: a player joining mid-round SPECTATES the current round (sees everything, controls nothing) until the next round-restart auto-spawns them; a disconnected player's bomber is HELD for 5 seconds before despawn, allowing tab refresh / network hiccup recovery; leaving deliberately (close tab) STILL despawns immediately. The drop-in/out model from `gdd.md` Multiplayer + `notes/DynaBomber.md §6.1` finally fully expresses.

Rationale:
Source: GDP-2026-05-22-009 acceptance hints (Sprint C bullet) + `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md §9.3` (drop-in/out rules with the spectate-until-next-round + 5s grace defaults already documented). After Sprint B's headline acceptance, this polish is what separates 'multiplayer prototype' from 'world that feels alive'. Without it, every refresh / unstable wifi user gets punished. Sized SHOULD because the headline gameplay works without it; Sprint C is essential polish, not a blocker.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Depends on GDP-2026-05-22-011 (Sprint B). Recipe + position sync are already shipped (S109+S112).
  - SPECTATE-UNTIL-NEXT-ROUND (mid-round join):
  -   Server tracks RoundState.phase. When a client.join arrives while phase ∈ {'playing'}:
  -     Server marks the new Presence entity with `pendingSpawn: true` and DOES NOT spawn a bomber for them in the current round.
  -     Client receives the snapshot; sees existing bombers + bombs + blasts; player input has no effect (no bomber attached).
  -     Client UI: a centre-bottom banner reads 'SPECTATING — joining next round'. Optional: a chevron above the spectator's would-be-spawn cell.
  -   When RoundState.phase flips to {'won', 'lost', 'draw'} → auto-restart fires → at the new round's spawn step, the pending-spawn presence becomes a real bomber spawned at the next available spawn cell.
  -   Multiple spectators waiting: spawn in entity-id order across the round-start.
  -   Edge case — no spawn cells available (4-player arena full): spectator KEEPS waiting through the round; server bumps player count target or simply holds them. Document in the spec which: recommend HOLD (no auto-promotion to mega-arena).
  - 5S RECONNECT GRACE (disconnect path):
  -   Server detects WebSocket close. Two cases:
  -     Deliberate close (client.leave message received before TCP close): despawn bomber IMMEDIATELY. Their live bombs continue to fuse + detonate (server-owned, no orphan cleanup).
  -     Network drop (TCP close without client.leave): mark Presence as `disconnected: true, disconnectedAt: now`. Hold the bomber in place for 5 seconds. Bomber is alive but frozen (input ignored, fuse on owned bombs continues, alive=false flip still possible via blast).
  -     If a client.join with the SAME playerId reconnects within 5s: clear disconnected flag, resume normal input → snap to wherever server says they are.
  -     If 5s elapses without reconnect: despawn the bomber (same as deliberate leave from there).
  -   Player ID continuity: client persists its assigned playerId in sessionStorage (NOT localStorage — same tab only) so a refresh-within-grace reconnects to the same bomber. New tab = new playerId, no auto-reclaim.
  - PROTOCOL EXTENSIONS:
  -   client.join: gains optional `resumePlayerId: string` field. Server validates: if playerId is in the disconnected-grace pool, resume; otherwise allocate new.
  -   client.leave: explicit deliberate-leave signal (sent before WebSocket close on graceful unmount). Existing protocol may already have this — verify.
  -   Snapshot: Presence entities gain `disconnected: boolean` + `pendingSpawn: boolean` fields. Clients use these to render the spectator UI + the disconnected-grayed-out marker on the minimap.
  - VISUAL TREATMENT:
  -   Spectator on the local client: HUD shows banner; minimap marker for self appears at the would-be-spawn cell in low-opacity.
  -   Disconnected bomber on REMOTE clients: bomber renders in greyscale (apply a desaturation tween to its mesh tree) for the 5s grace. Pops back to full colour on reconnect. Visual cue that 'this player is having connection trouble'.
  -   Local-disconnect view: the local client may show a 'reconnecting...' overlay if the WebSocket reports disconnect — graceful UX. Not strictly required for the server-side rules; recommend.
  - ROUND-RESOLVE INTERACTION:
  -   If a player disconnects mid-round → 5s grace freezes their bomber → round ends mid-grace (e.g. opponent kills them, or timeout). Round-resolve fires NORMALLY. The frozen disconnected bomber counts as alive for tally purposes UNLESS killed by a blast during the grace (alive-flip still works on grace-frozen bombers).
  -   Per gameplay-systems.md §6.4 'no full-world reset on player leave': leaving mid-round does NOT abort the round.
  - DETERMINISM:
  -   Spectator queue order is by entity-id, deterministic.
  -   5s grace timer is wall-clock on the server (not tick-based — the server's tick rate may differ from clients').
  -   Reconnect resumption is idempotent: same playerId always resumes to the same bomber.
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:
  -   Tab A starts round; 5 seconds into the round, Tab B joins → Tab B sees 'SPECTATING' banner; Tab A's player runs around normally → at round-resolve + auto-restart, Tab B spawns as a real bomber.
  -   Tab A refreshes mid-round → Tab B sees Tab A's bomber go grey for ≤ 5s, then resume colour as Tab A's refreshed session reconnects → no double-spawn.
  -   Tab A closes intentionally (clicks browser close button — sends client.leave) → Tab B sees Tab A's bomber despawn immediately; Tab A's live bombs continue to fuse + detonate.
  -   Tab A loses wifi for 8 seconds → Tab B sees grey for 5s then despawn → Tab A reconnects after grace expires → Tab A enters as a fresh spectator awaiting next round.
  - OUT OF SCOPE:
  -   Persistent sessions across full server restart (server reboot loses the in-grace pool — acceptable).
  -   Cross-device session migration (mobile ↔ desktop with same playerId).
  -   Friend invites / private rooms / room codes.
  -   Reconnect grace beyond 5s configurability per server (5s is hardcoded for the first cut).
  -   Spawn-cell starvation auto-promotion (4 max bombers; spectators just queue).

Source proposal: GDP-2026-05-22-012 (kind=feature, priority=should)
stories.deferredReason: Depends on FEAT-MULTIPLAYER-SPRINT-B-SER-001. Can't ship reconnect-grace before the server owns gameplay state. Re-promote alongside or after Sprint B.

stories.title: Texturing Layer 3 — shader-side stripe/spot patterns via MeshStandardMaterial.onBeforeCompile injection
stories.summary:
Layer 1 (panel seams, S109) and Layer 2 (body decals, S112) shipped via vertex-color attribute writes — cheap and additive. Layer 3 is the remaining piece of the original GDP-2026-05-21-004 spec: family-flavour stripe and spot patterns mixed in via the SHADER side. Patterns are driven by mesh local coordinates + a `recipe.texturing.pattern` field. They differ from Layer 1/2 because they're not per-vertex — they're per-fragment, sampled procedurally. This is the visual flavour that turns palette-distinct bombers into pattern-distinct bombers: 'ember' family with horizontal stripes reads differently from 'mint' family with polka spots, beyond just hue. Deferred from S112 specifically because it needs `MeshStandardMaterial.onBeforeCompile` injection, which is a shader-pipeline surface dev hadn't touched yet in Kaboom Crew.

Rationale:
Source: original GDP-2026-05-21-004 (Layer 3 specifications) + S112 sprint notes ('Texturing Layer 3 (shader-side stripes/spots) remains deferred — needs onBeforeCompile injection on MeshStandardMaterial, more shader-side scope than fits this sprint'). Conditions for un-defer are now met — Layer 1+2 shipped, no surprises in the vertex-color path, the shader work is well-isolated. Marked `could` because Layer 1+2 already deliver the bulk of the per-bomber visual identity gain; Layer 3 is the cherry on top.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Depends on Layers 1+2 (panel seams + decals, both shipped). No new vertex attribute work; this is pure fragment-shader.
  - Recipe surface: `recipe.texturing.pattern: { style: 'solid' | 'stripes' | 'spots', scale: 0.5..3.0 } | undefined` — already in the CharacterRecipe schema (added during GDP-007 Layer 1 schema work, but un-consumed until this layer ships).
  - SHADER INJECTION POINT:
  -   Use Three.js `MeshStandardMaterial` + `material.onBeforeCompile = (shader) => { ... }` to splice in a fragment-shader snippet that modulates the diffuse colour.
  -   Add 4 uniforms via onBeforeCompile:
  -     uPatternStyle (int)  — 0=solid, 1=stripes, 2=spots
  -     uPatternScale (float) — cycles per local unit (0.5..3.0)
  -     uPatternColor (vec3)  — palette.torsoAccent as vec3 (already a palette channel)
  -     uPatternStrength (float) — mix amount, hardcoded 0.3 for v1
  -   Vertex shader: pass local position (vPosLocal) to fragment.
  -   Fragment shader insert (after the diffuse colour resolves, before lighting):
  -     stripes: `if (uPatternStyle == 1) { float s = sin(vPosLocal.y * uPatternScale * 6.28318); if (s > 0.0) diffuseColor.rgb = mix(diffuseColor.rgb, uPatternColor, uPatternStrength); }`
  -     spots: `if (uPatternStyle == 2) { vec2 c = floor(vPosLocal.xz * uPatternScale); float h = fract(sin(dot(c, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453); if (h > 0.75) diffuseColor.rgb = mix(diffuseColor.rgb, uPatternColor, uPatternStrength); }`
  -     solid: no-op (default).
  - AFFECTED MESHES:
  -   Pattern applies to torso + head + upperArm × 2 + forearm × 2 + upperLeg × 2 + lowerLeg × 2 = 10 body meshes per bomber. Accessories STAY solid-coloured (silhouette discipline per visual-style.md).
  -   Apply via per-part material variant or via a shared material with per-mesh uniform overrides. Dev's call — shared material with InstancedMesh-style overrides is leaner if all-bomber-meshes share one material. Per-mesh material instance is simpler if not.
  - FAMILY-DEFAULT PATTERN BIAS (drives identity per palette family):
  -   ember → stripes (warm horizontal bands)
  -   mint  → spots (cool polka)
  -   plum  → spots (cool polka, different from mint via colour)
  -   sky   → stripes
  -   sand  → solid (neutral)
  -   jade  → spots
  -   rose  → stripes
  -   slate → solid (neutral)
  -   bomber-palette.ts gains a `patternBias` field per family; resolveCharacterRecipe uses it when recipe.texturing.pattern is unspecified.
  - BENCH UI: extend the existing Texturing section in the procbomber-bench panel with:
  -   Dropdown: 'Pattern style' — solid / stripes / spots
  -   Slider: 'Pattern scale' — 0.5..3.0
  -   Live-rebuild on change (the material uniform path; no geometry rebuild needed for pure shader-uniform updates).
  - UNIT TESTS:
  -   Schema validation: pattern.style enum strict, scale clamped.
  -   Family bias: 200 random seeds → each family produces its biased pattern unless overridden.
  -   Determinism: same seed → same resolved pattern.
  -   Snapshot test on the resolved material uniforms (catches accidental drift in the bias table).
  - PERFORMANCE:
  -   No new draw calls. ~6 extra ALU ops per fragment for stripes (sin + threshold + mix), ~10 for spots (hash + threshold + mix). Negligible.
  -   Uniform update on recipe change only — steady-state cost zero.
  - VISUAL QA (manual):
  -   Load 8 family-default bombers in the bench → each family's pattern is visually distinct (stripes vs spots vs solid).
  -   Override one bomber to spots with scale 0.5 → polka dots are large. Override to scale 3.0 → small dense dots.
  -   Layer 1+2 still work alongside Layer 3 — panel seams + decals + pattern all readable simultaneously without overload.
  - ACCESSORIES INTERACTION:
  -   Accessories from S106 use a DIFFERENT material profile (or the same material with uPatternStyle=0). They stay solid-coloured per visual-style.md §3.1 silhouette discipline.
  - OUT OF SCOPE:
  -   Animated patterns (flowing emissive, scrolling stripes). Separate shader profile if ever needed.
  -   Per-vertex pattern overrides (e.g. only chest has stripes). The whole bomber shares one pattern.
  -   Pattern editor in the bench (no authorable preview beyond the dropdown + scale slider).
  -   Pattern variants beyond stripes / spots (checkerboard, gradient, herringbone, etc.). Three patterns is the design budget; future patterns are one-at-a-time follow-ups.

Source proposal: GDP-2026-05-22-013 (kind=feature, priority=could)
stories.deferredReason: S113 shipped stripes via vertex-color. Shader-side stripes + spots need MeshStandardMaterial.onBeforeCompile injection - a moderate shader-infrastructure investment. Re-promote in a dedicated visuals sprint.

stories.title: Match structure — best-of-3 rounds + match-resolve banner + tally reset (MVP-2 session transition)
stories.summary:
Kaboom Crew is currently an endless-round-loop game: rounds resolve, tally bumps, auto-restart fires, repeat forever. `gdd.md §Round structure (planned, MVP-2)` documented the intended next step: a 'match' = best-of-3 decisive rounds. When the tally reaches the threshold (default 3 decisive rounds, draws don't count), a MATCH-RESOLVED banner shows, the tally resets to 0/0/0, and a longer pause precedes the next match. This adds session shape — a clear endpoint, a clear winner per match — without complicating the existing round mechanics. Critical for multiplayer where players want a 'natural break' moment to leave / refresh / etc. without losing their progress.

Rationale:
Source: `docs/game-design/gdd.md` Round structure planned-MVP-2 section + `gameplay-systems.md §6.3` ('A match is a best-of-3 rounds. When tally.player + tally.bot + tally.draws reaches a configurable target...'). The current endless loop was the right MVP-1 shape but starts to feel unstructured once players hang around for many rounds. Multiplayer especially benefits: players who join, want a clear 'play 1 match then leave' arc. Sized `should` because the existing endless loop continues to work — match structure is polish on top. Coordinates cleanly with multiplayer Sprint B+C: matches become natural drop-in/out boundaries (spectate-until-next-MATCH instead of spectate-until-next-ROUND for some scenarios).

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Does NOT depend on multiplayer Sprint B/C; can ship in solo mode first and extend when multiplayer landed.
  - Schema: a new MatchState singleton component (mirrors RoundState's pattern). Lives on the kaboom.game-state entity.
  -   MatchState { phase: 'playing' | 'resolved', target: integer (default 3), resolved_at?: number, last_match_winner?: 'player' | 'bot' | 'draw' }
  - RoundResolveSystem extends: after bumping tally, check if `max(tally.player, tally.bot) >= MatchState.target`. If so → MatchState.phase = 'resolved', last_match_winner = whoever hit target (or 'draw' if tied after target rounds — rare with best-of-3).
  - MATCH-RESOLVED behaviour:
  -   Normal auto-restart pauses MatchState-aware: when MatchState.phase = 'resolved', the post-round pause extends from 3s to 7s (configurable). Gives the match-end banner time to land + audience to process.
  -   After the extended pause: MatchState.phase = 'playing', tally resets to 0/0/0, RoundState.roundNumber resets to 1. Scene reload as normal.
  -   RoundState.roundNumber resets per-match, NOT per-game. The 'I am on round 5 of the current match' read becomes 'round 5 / 3 of match N'.
  - HUD CHANGES:
  -   Bottom-left tally line gains a match indicator: `Match 3 | Round 2/3 | W:1 L:1 D:0` (or compact equivalent).
  -   Centre banner on match-resolve: 'MATCH 3 — YOU WIN' / 'MATCH 3 — YOU LOSE' / 'MATCH 3 — DRAW'. Visually distinct from per-round banner (larger text, longer hold).
  -   Match-resolve banner colour from `visual-style.md §5.2` (H3 green for player-win, H0 red for player-loss, H1 orange for draw — reuse round-resolve banner palette).
  - PERSISTENT MATCH NUMBER:
  -   MatchState gains a `matchNumber: integer` that increments each match. Survives auto-restart same as RoundState.roundNumber+tally already do (via bootstrap restartScene re-seed).
  -   HUD shows current match number — gives the round-after-round feel a hierarchical structure.
  - URL CONFIG:
  -   `?matchTarget=N` overrides the default best-of-3 → best-of-N (1 = single round wins match; 5 = best-of-5; useful for tournaments).
  - AUDIO:
  -   Match-resolve fires a longer fanfare than round-resolve. New audio event: `match-resolved` distinct from `round-resolved`.
  -   Vocal-synth (GDP-008 / shipped S110) victory slot also fires for the MATCH winner, not just the round winner. Slightly extends the speech-like utterance for impact.
  - MULTIPLAYER COORDINATION (forward-compatible):
  -   When multiplayer Sprint C (GDP-2026-05-22-012) lands, spectate-until-next-MATCH becomes an optional join policy (server-config flag). For long matches it's nicer than spectate-until-next-round; for short matches it's overkill. Default stays per-round; per-match is opt-in.
  -   Server is authoritative on MatchState same as RoundState. Both flip in lockstep via snapshot.
  - DETERMINISM:
  -   Match-resolve check is deterministic — based on tally comparison only. Same gameplay → same match outcomes.
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:
  -   Solo mode: play 3 rounds, win 2 of 3 → match-resolve banner fires + 7s pause + new match starts with tally 0/0/0 and matchNumber 2.
  -   Draws don't count: play 5 rounds with 2 wins + 2 losses + 1 draw → no match resolve yet; round 6 with a win → match resolves at 3 wins.
  -   Best-of-1: ?matchTarget=1 → every round-resolve is a match-resolve.
  -   HUD reads naturally during play — players can tell which round of which match they're on.
  - OUT OF SCOPE:
  -   Sets / series / tournaments (best-of-3 matches comprise a set, etc.). Single match is the unit.
  -   Match history / leaderboard (no persistent profile yet).
  -   Custom match-resolve celebrations (animations, fireworks). Banner + audio + vocal is enough for MVP-2.
  -   Per-arena match-target override (one global ?matchTarget for now).
  -   Spectator-only mode (separate to spectate-until-next-round mid-round join).

Source proposal: GDP-2026-05-22-014 (kind=feature, priority=should)
verification: acceptance: Kaboom Crew gains match structure. New MatchState singleton on kaboom.game-state entity: { phase: 'playing'|'resolved', target: integer (default 3), matchNumber, lastMatchWinner: 'player'|'bot'|'draw', resolvedAt }. RoundResolveSystem writes MatchState on every tally bump; flips phase='resolved' when max(tally) >= target. Auto-restart pause extends from 3s to 7s (configurable) when match resolved. On next match: tally resets, roundNumber=1, matchNumber++. HUD stats line: 'Match N | Round R/T   W:n L:n D:n'. Centre banner copy reads 'MATCH N — YOU WIN' (etc) with the next-match-in-7s hint. ?matchTarget=N URL param overrides default best-of-3.
